question: Does a write-capable agent on this host land in a checkout that is separate from the parent's worktree and index, and does its own git work still succeed there?
why_a_probe_and_not_a_test: The spawn is issued by an agent, not by a script. Probe 2026-07-10-issue-430 recorded `no host-exposed automated spawn-denial probe surface found`, so spawn PLACEMENT is on the same standing as envelope binding and result delivery: proven per host by observation, never by a suite assertion. The suite proves the property of a checkout; it cannot prove where a spawn went.

observations.git_worktree_list_confirms_linked: both appear in `git worktree list` on their own branches (worktree-agent-<id>), each with its own HEAD distinct from the parent's
observations.agent_worktrees_are_gitignored: .gitignore:52 `.claude/worktrees/`, so an agent's tree cannot reach the parent's commit through an untracked path either

verdict: This host does place some agents in real linked git worktrees, and `charness worktree doctor --require-isolation` renders PASS against such a worktree and FAIL against the main one.
non_claims: Does NOT establish that the agents occupying these worktrees were WRITE-CAPABLE, nor that isolation was REQUESTED rather than a host default. Both are inferences from the worktrees' existence; nothing observed here shows the spawn parameters or the agent's tool surface. An earlier draft of this record asserted `isolation-requested spawns` as if measured -- a round-1 reviewer refuted it, and the correction is kept rather than silently rewritten.
Does NOT prove the host isolates a spawn that did not ask for isolation, which is why the read-only shared-tree hygiene rule still stands for reviewers.
Does NOT prove or disprove behavior on any other host. Per-host, by construction.
Does NOT establish that this session's own reviewer spawns were isolated; it establishes that the mechanism exists and is observable on this host.
The observed worktrees were created by earlier sessions and read here as evidence; this probe did not itself spawn a write-capable agent to create one.

Does NOT discharge the SECOND half of SC10's acceptance check. That half -- `reviewer_boundary_fingerprint verify` over a window containing such a spawn returning no UNDECLARED drift -- is recorded separately in the S6 closeout, not here. A reader mapping acceptance to evidence must not read this probe as covering it.
The FAIL direction was rendered against the MAIN worktree, not against an agent worktree; `doctor_command` below records the command for the PASS direction only.
negative_case_covered_by_suite: tests/charness_cli/test_worktree_doctor.py::test_a_linked_worktree_is_isolated_and_its_own_commits_still_succeed asserts `git add`/`commit`/`checkout -b` SUCCEED inside a linked worktree while the main worktree's HEAD, index, and working tree do not move. STATED HONESTLY after a round-1 reviewer refuted the first wording: that assertion is a property of GIT, not a regression guard on charness code -- delete the isolation check entirely and it still passes. What the test pins is the DEFINITION of isolation this repo uses; it cannot catch the failure mode the ruling names (an agent whose shell was taken away), because no suite can exercise that.
